title: Rationality of the zeta series
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a scheme of finite type (quasi-compact and locally of finite
type) over $\Fq$. Then there are $A,B\in\Z[T]$ with $B(0)=1$ and

$$
B(T)\,Z(X_0,T)=A(T)\quad\text{in }\Q[[T]];
$$

in particular $Z(X_0,T)\in\Q(T)\cap(1+T\Z[[T]])$.

proof.text: The original first sentence invokes the theorem sk-thm-tracetodeterminant, which assumes smoothness, properness and geometric connectedness; these hypotheses are absent here. For example, $X_0=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_q}$ satisfies this theorem's hypothesis but is not proper, and a line with doubled origin is an allowed nonseparated example. We repair that inapplicable inference using compact supports on affine pieces, without adding any hypothesis. The finite field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X_0$ Noetherian. By [lem-zl-affine-partition], choose a finite partition $X_0=\coprod_{j=1}^sY_{0,j}$ by locally closed reduced affine subschemes. Each inclusion is locally of finite type by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]; composition remains locally of finite type by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], applied to the affine source and the affine field spectrum, writing $Y_{0,j}=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ gives a finitely generated $\mathbf F_q$-algebra $B_j$. The single affine chart is then the finite affine cover required by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so $Y_{0,j}$ is finite type over $\mathbf F_q$. It is separated over that field by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Empty pieces may be discarded; if $X_0$ is empty, the empty partition is allowed.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); affine partition: main blueprint lem-zl-affine-partition; separatedness: Schemes Tag 01KN; Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize)

proof.text: For every finite extension $L/\mathbf F_q$, every $L$-valued point of $X_0$ factors through exactly one $Y_{0,j}$. Indeed, its image $x$ lies in exactly one stratum. Write that stratum as a reduced closed subscheme of an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$. The point factors through $U$, since its inverse image is all of $\operatorname{Spec}L$. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$ of $x$, let $I\subseteq A$ define the stratum and let $\alpha:A\to L$ define the point. Membership $x\in V(I)$ says $I\subseteq\ker\alpha$, so $\alpha$ factors uniquely through $A/I$. This gives a factorization through the stratum; it is unique because the quotient map is surjective and the open restriction is unique. Thus $X_0(L)=\coprod_jY_{0,j}(L)$ as sets. These sets are finite by [lem-weil-point-counts-finite]. Consequently $N_n(X_0)=\sum_jN_n(Y_{0,j})$ for every $n\geq1$. Substituting this equality into the exponential definition [sk-def-zeta] and applying the finite-sum identity [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] gives $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_jZ(Y_{0,j},T)$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. The empty sum gives $Z(\varnothing,T)=1$.

source.place: The first-cover-member partition; point-factorization argument supplied here; exponential finite-sum rule as in Milne Theorem 27.6, p. 156

proof.text: The series of [prop-euler-product] is the zeta series of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta]; for a finite-type $\mathbf F_q$-scheme it is the series $Z$ of [sk-def-zeta] used here. Both are $\exp(\sum_{n\geq1}N_nT^n/n)$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$ with $N_n=\#\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf F_q}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},-)$. In the first, $\mathbf F_{q^n}$ is the splitting field of $T^{q^n}-T$, realized in $k$ as $\{a:a^{q^n}=a\}$; in the second it is the subfield of $k$ with $q^n$ elements. These are the same subfield, so the two Hom sets coincide. The convention of [sk-def-zeta] that $N_n=0$ for an infinite set never applies, since [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] states that these sets are finite for finite-type schemes. Both nodes define $\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$. Apply [prop-euler-product] to the original finite-type scheme $X_0$ and separately to each $Y_{0,j}$. It yields $Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ and $Z(Y_{0,j},T)=\prod_{y\in|Y_{0,j}|}(1-T^{\deg(y)})^{-1}$, with coefficientwise locally finite products. In particular the coefficients $z_n$ of $Z(X_0,T)=\sum_{n\geq0}z_nT^n$ are integers and $z_0=1$.

source.place: Closed-point product and integrality for every finite-type scheme

proof.text: Choose a prime $\ell\ne p$ (use $2$ unless $p=2$, then $3$), put $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and set $Y_j=Y_{0,j}\times_{k_0}k$. By [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum] the constant adic object $E_{Y_j}$ has its normalized model and geometric Weil maps. Apply [lem-zl-assumed-trace-determinant-bridge]: first realize it as $J_{Y_j}(E_{Y_j})$ over the condensed ring $E_{Y_j}^c$, then extend along the coefficient map of [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map] to $K_j=U_{Y_j}\otimes^L_{E_{Y_j}^c}J_{Y_j}(E_{Y_j})\cong U_{Y_j}$. Its unit pullback map $\phi_j$ gives the actual WeilBoundedConstructibleOfEnd required by [nt-assume-trace-formula]. The geometric base change is separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to the stratum from Step 1. Denote its compact-support comparison by $\sigma_j:Ra_{Y_j!}^{\mathrm{cond}}K_j\cong\rho_{E,s}(C_{E,j})$, with $C_{E,j}=R\Gamma_c(Y_j,E)$.

source.place: First sentence, repaired compact-support factorization on each separated affine stratum; explicit condensed-coefficient bridge under the batch-5 assumption

proof.text: For every $m\ge1$, [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] identifies the fixed $k$-points of $\Phi_j^m$ with $Y_{0,j}(\mathbf F_{q^m})$; [lem-weil-point-counts-finite] gives their finiteness. Independently, [prop-cohomological-finiteness] says $C_{E,j}$ has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology. The realization and stalk comparisons of [lem-zl-assumed-trace-determinant-bridge], together with the right-dual assertion of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace], therefore give right duals of $Ra_{Y_j!}^{\mathrm{cond}}K_j$ and every stalk $Lx^*K_j\cong U_s$. Thus all hypotheses of [nt-assume-trace-formula] hold, including HasRightDual in its actual condensed category. Ordinary finiteness is used as input to the realization theorem; it is not itself a right-dual assertion.

source.place: First sentence, repaired compact-support factorization on each separated affine stratum; explicit condensed-coefficient bridge under the batch-5 assumption

proof.text:
Apply [nt-assume-trace-formula] to $(K_j,\phi_{j,m})$. By [lem-zl-condensed-global-frobenius-comparison], its global operator $G_{j,m}$ satisfies $\sigma_jG_{j,m}=\rho_{E,s}(F_j^m)\sigma_j$, with $F_j$ exactly the geometric operator on $C_{E,j}$. By [lem-zl-assumed-trace-determinant-bridge] every fixed-point stalk operator is the identity of $U_s$. The trace assertion of [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] now turns the assumed equality, in $\operatorname{End}(U_s)$, into
$$\epsilon_E\left(\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}_E(F_j^m\mid H_c^i(Y_j,E))\right)=\epsilon_E\bigl(\#Y_{0,j}(\mathbf F_{q^m})\bigr).$$
The sum of local traces equals the right side since each is $\epsilon_E(1)$ and $\epsilon_E$ is additive. Its injectivity, stated in the same point-supertrace lemma, gives the ordinary $E$-valued trace identity. No functor from condensed objects back to adic objects is being presumed.

source.place: First sentence, repaired compact-support factorization on each separated affine stratum; explicit condensed-coefficient bridge under the batch-5 assumption

proof.text:
Write $V_{i,j}=H_c^i(Y_j,E)$ and $P_{i,j}(T)=\det(1-TF_j\mid V_{i,j})$. Only finitely many $V_{i,j}$ are nonzero by [prop-cohomological-finiteness]. Substitute the trace identities of Step 6 into the exponential defining $Z$ in [sk-def-zeta]. The coefficientwise homomorphism [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map] sends its exponential to the exponential over $E$: coefficient $n$ of the exponential is a finite sum of products with rational coefficients, so applying a $\mathbf Q$-algebra map commutes term by term. The finite-sum rule of [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] separates the degrees $i$, and [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant] gives
$$\iota Z(Y_{0,j},T)=\prod_iP_{i,j}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\quad\text{in }E[[T]].$$
Indeed each exponential $\exp(\sum_{m\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(F_j^m\mid V_{i,j})T^m/m)$ equals $P_{i,j}^{-1}$; the sign $(-1)^i$ in the exponent produces $P_{i,j}^{(-1)^{i+1}}$. This proves the determinant identity in the item itself.

source.place: First sentence, repaired compact-support factorization on each separated affine stratum; explicit condensed-coefficient bridge under the batch-5 assumption

proof.text: For each $j$, the determinant product in Step 7 is finite because [prop-cohomological-finiteness] gives finite-dimensional compact-support cohomology vanishing outside a finite interval. Define $A_{j,\ell}$ as the product of the odd-degree determinants and $B_{j,\ell}$ as the product of the even-degree determinants. Each determinant has constant term $1$, hence $A_{j,\ell},B_{j,\ell}\in E[T]$ have constant term $1$ and satisfy $B_{j,\ell}\,\iota Z(Y_{0,j},T)=A_{j,\ell}$.

source.place: first sentence expanded by the batch-5 categorical-trace bridge for each separated affine stratum

proof.text: Set $A_\ell=\prod_jA_{j,\ell}$ and $B_\ell=\prod_jB_{j,\ell}$ in $E[T]$. Multiply the finitely many identities from Step 8 and use the product identity of Step 2. The coefficientwise map is a ring homomorphism by [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map], so $B_\ell\,\iota Z(X_0,T)=A_\ell$ and $B_\ell(0)=\prod_j1=1$. Empty products equal $1$. Thus the image of $Z(X_0,T)$ has a normalized rational presentation over $E$.

source.place: First sentence, finite rational product; now the compact-support product over the affine partition

proof.text: By [prop-weil-rationality-criterion], the presentation in Step 9 implies finite Hankel rank over $E$: there is an integer $r\geq0$ bounding the ranks of all finite square submatrices of $(\iota(z_{a+b}))_{a,b\geq0}$. This is exactly the finite-submatrix meaning of Hankel rank in [def-weil-hankel-matrix]. Since $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ has characteristic zero by [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], $\mathbf Q\hookrightarrow E$ is a field extension. For every finite square submatrix $M=(z_{a+b})$ with entries in $\mathbf Q$ (indeed in $\mathbf Z$ by Step 3), [lem-weil-matrix-rank-field-extension] gives $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Q}M=\operatorname{rank}_{E}\iota(M)\leq r$. Therefore the Hankel rank of the original rational-coefficient series is finite as well. This compares each finite matrix; it does not assert a base-change theorem for an infinite product of vector spaces.

source.place: Lemma 27.9, pp. 156–157, descent of the Hankel determinant/rank condition

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-rationality-criterion] once more, now over $\mathbf Q$, to the finite Hankel rank from Step 10. There are $a,b\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $b(0)=1$ and $bZ(X_0,T)=a$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. In particular $Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T)$.

source.place: Last two sentences: rationality criterion over the prime field

proof.text: Step 3 gives $Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ and Step 11 gives rationality over $\mathbf Q$. Apply [prop-weil-integral-rational-series], the integral Fatou theorem, to this series. It produces $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $A(0)=B(0)=1$ and $BZ=A$; the theorem even supplies coprimality and uniqueness, which are not required here. Apply the coefficientwise inclusions [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map] and the polynomial inclusion [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series] to read that identity in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. This proves the requested integral presentation and the final membership $Z\in\mathbf Q(T)\cap(1+T\mathbf Z[[T]])$. Merely clearing the denominators of the rational polynomials in Step 11 would not justify $B(0)=1$; the Fatou input supplies precisely this missing normalization.

source.place: Normalized integral presentation (missing from the imported rationality proof); compare Milne Proposition 27.11, p. 158

tool_uses.why: Finite affine partition of the Noetherian source, needed to apply the separated compact-support formula without imposing separatedness on X_0; no node in the rationality unit supplies it.
Finite-dimensionality and boundedness of compact cohomology for the constant E-Weil sheaf on each separated finite-type stratum; the smooth-proper family does not provide these groups.

Step 10 compares the rank of each finite integral Hankel submatrix over Q and over Q_l. This generic linear-algebra fact (rank unchanged by field extension) is stated by no node in the rationality unit's route, whose source paragraph asserts it inline.
Only the fixed-point/rational-point identification is used to verify a hypothesis of the assumed trace formula; no trace-formula proof is invoked.
Checks that the geometric fibre lies in the domain of the condensed functors; a generic scheme base-change property, not a duality theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem zetaSeries_rational [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ P Q : Polynomial ℤ, Q.coeff 0 = 1 ∧
      f.zetaSeries * (Q.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) : PowerSeries ℚ) =
        (P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) : PowerSeries ℚ)
lean.note: Exact existing upstream statement in WeilConjectures.Statement.lean: Dwork rationality for every finite-type scheme over a finite field. The explicit morphism f, [LocallyOfFiniteType f] and [QuasiCompact f], integral polynomials P and Q, normalization Q.coeff 0 = 1, and equality in PowerSeries ℚ match the node verbatim. The upstream theorem body is sorry in the source branch and is reused as the recorded declaration; no duplicate module is written.
